claims.text: What the image looks like Bone scan: diffuse skull/pelvis uptake = Paget disease
claims.quote: Diffuse skull/pelvis uptake = Paget disease

claims.text: Radiographs are required to confirm: osteolysis, abnormal architecture with coarse trabeculae and cortical thickening and sclerosis; involved bone may be enlarged, and lesions in the tibia or femur may result in bowing
claims.quote: Confirmation on radiographs is required to establish the diagnosis. Characteristic radiographic findings include osteolysis, abnormal architecture with coarse trabeculae and cortical thickening and sclerosis. Involved bone may be enlarged, and pagetic lesions in the tibia or femur may result in bowing.

claims.text: Example skull radiograph: a typical mosaic pattern of areas of increased sclerosis and lucency; these cotton-wool patches result from thickening of the calvarium
claims.quote: A typical mosaic pattern of areas of increased sclerosis and lucency is seen in this radiograph. These cotton-wool patches result from thickening of the calvarium.
claims.locator: Radiograph of the Skull in Paget Disease image caption

claims.text: Example pelvis radiograph: pelvic bones with a mottled appearance due to increased porosity, with secondary osteoarthritis of the hip
claims.quote: The pelvic bones in this radiograph have a mottled appearance due to their increased porosity, coexisting with secondary osteoarthritis of the hip
claims.locator: Radiograph of the Pelvis in Paget Disease image caption

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) When suspected from imaging or bone-origin alkaline phosphatase, a radionuclide bone scan using technetium-labeled phosphonates should be done to determine the extent of bone involvement; with diagnostic uncertainty, biopsy should be performed to exclude metastatic disease
claims.quote: When Paget disease is suspected based on imaging findings or elevated alkaline phosphatase of bone origin, a radionuclide bone scan using technetium-labeled phosphonates should be done to determine the extent of bone involvement. In cases of diagnostic uncertainty, a biopsy should be performed to exclude possible metastatic disease.

claims.text: Any bone can be involved: most commonly the pelvis, femur and skull; less commonly the tibia, vertebrae, clavicle and humerus; involvement is usually asymmetric
claims.quote: Any bone can be involved in Paget disease. The bones most commonly affected are the pelvis, femur, and skull. Other less commonly involved bones are the tibia, vertebrae, clavicle, and humerus. The bone involvement is usually asymmetric.

claims.text: Labs: elevated serum alkaline phosphatase but usually normal serum gamma-glutamyl-transpeptidase (GGT), 5'-nucleotidase and phosphate; serum calcium usually normal (may be increased if immobilized); if hypercalcemia is present, evaluate for concurrent hyperparathyroidism
claims.quote: Characteristic laboratory findings include elevated serum alkaline phosphatase (increased anabolic activity of bone) but usually normal serum gamma-glutamyl-transpeptidase (GGT), 5'-nucleotidase, and serum phosphate levels. Serum calcium is usually normal, though it may be increased in patients who are immobilized. If hypercalcemia is present, the patient should be evaluated for concurrent hyperparathyroidism.

claims.text: Pearl: consider Paget disease of bone in older adults with persistently elevated alkaline phosphatase but normal gamma-glutamyl-transpeptidase
claims.quote: Consider Paget disease of bone in older adults with persistently elevated alkaline phosphatase but normal gamma-glutamyl-transpeptidase levels.

claims.text: Causes A late-onset chronic disorder of the adult skeleton in which bone turnover is accelerated in localized areas; normal matrix is replaced with softened and enlarged bone
claims.quote: Paget disease of bone is a late-onset chronic disorder of the adult skeleton in which bone turnover is accelerated in localized areas. Normal matrix is replaced with softened and enlarged bone.

claims.text: Mechanism: pagetic lesions are metabolically active and highly vascular; excessively active osteoclasts are often large with many nuclei; hyperactive osteoblastic repair causes coarsely woven, thickened lamellae and trabeculae, weakening the bone despite enlargement and areas of sclerosis
claims.quote: Bone turnover is accelerated at involved sites. Pagetic lesions are metabolically active and highly vascular. Excessively active osteoclasts are often large and contain many nuclei. Osteoblastic repair is also hyperactive, causing coarsely woven, thickened lamellae and trabeculae. This abnormal structure weakens the bone, despite bone enlargement and areas of bone sclerosis.

claims.text: A genetic component (familial clustering in 15 to 30% of patients, autosomal dominant with incomplete penetrance) has been reported; approximately 10% have pathogenic SQSTM1 variants that increase osteoclast activity
claims.quote: A genetic component of the disease characterized by a familial clustering in 15 to 30% of patients and an autosomal dominant pattern of inheritance with incomplete penetrance has been reported (1). Approximately 10% of patients with Paget disease have pathogenic variants of the SQSTM1 (sequestosome-1) gene, resulting in increased nuclear factor kappa-B activity in osteoclasts, which increases osteoclast activity (1).

claims.text: A viral etiology, such as measles, has been proposed but remains controversial; it is hypothesized that in genetically predisposed patients an unidentified virus or other environmental factors may trigger abnormal osteoclast activity
claims.quote: A viral etiology, such as measles, has been proposed because nuclear inclusions in diseased osteoclasts that are similar to those seen in paramyxovirus-infected cells have been seen on electron microscopy. Although a viral cause remains controversial, it is hypothesized that in genetically predisposed patients an as yet unidentified virus or other environmental factors may trigger abnormal osteoclast activity (5).

claims.text: Symptoms Often asymptomatic; if symptoms occur, they develop insidiously with pain, stiffness, fatigue, and rarely bone deformity; bone pain is aching, deep, occasionally severe, sometimes worse at night
claims.quote: Paget disease of bone is often asymptomatic. If symptoms occur, they develop insidiously, with pain, stiffness, fatigue, and rarely bone deformity. Bone pain is aching, deep, and occasionally severe, sometimes worse at night.

claims.text: If the skull is involved, signs may include skull enlargement bitemporally and frontally (frontal bossing), dilated scalp veins and hearing loss; symptoms may include vertigo, headaches and hearing impairment; deformities may develop from bowing of the long bones or osteoarthritis; pathologic fractures may be the presenting manifestation; new onset or severe pain at a site of pagetic bone should prompt consideration of osteosarcoma
claims.quote: If the skull is involved, signs may include skull enlargement bitemporally and frontally (frontal bossing), dilated scalp veins, and hearing loss (sensorineural, conductive, or mixed) in one or both ears. Symptoms may include vertigo, headaches, and hearing impairment. Deformities may develop from bowing of the long bones or osteoarthritis. Pathologic fractures may be the presenting manifestation. New onset or severe pain at a site of pagetic bone should prompt consideration of osteosarcoma.

claims.text: Osteoarthritis occurs in up to 50% of patients, in joints adjacent to involved bone; pathologic fracture is also common
claims.quote: Osteoarthritis occurs in up to 50% of patients and develops in joints adjacent to involved bone (1). Pathologic fracture is also common due to focal areas of weakened bone and bone bowing.

claims.text: Complications can include osteoarthritis, fractures, neural compression, hypercalcemia, and rarely osteosarcoma
claims.quote: Complications can include osteoarthritis, fractures, neural compression, hypercalcemia, and rarely osteosarcoma.

claims.text: Treatment and next step Supportive care for symptoms and complications; bisphosphonates if bone disease is symptomatic or active in bones at risk of complications
claims.quote: Supportive care for symptoms and complications Bisphosphonates if bone disease is symptomatic or active in bones at risk of complications

claims.text: First-line treatment is bisphosphonates, preferably zoledronic acid
claims.quote: First-line treatment is with bisphosphonates, preferably zoledronic acid.

claims.text: Supportive: analgesics or NSAIDs for pain; orthotics to correct abnormal gait from bowed lower extremities; some patients require orthopedic surgery (eg, hip or knee replacement; decompression of the spinal cord); weight bearing should be encouraged and bed rest avoided
claims.quote: Supportive treatment of Paget disease of bone includes analgesics or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for pain. Orthotics help correct abnormal gait caused by bowed lower extremities. Some patients require orthopedic surgery (eg, hip or knee replacement, which may give rise to increased risk of medical and surgical complications [1]; decompression of the spinal cord). Weight bearing should be encouraged, and bed rest should be avoided.

claims.text: Localized, asymptomatic disease may not require treatment
claims.quote: Localized, asymptomatic disease may not require treatment.

claims.text: Some guidelines also recommend treatment to prevent or slow progression of complications (particularly when surgery is not appropriate), to prevent or minimize bleeding if orthopedic surgery is planned at a pagetic site, and to suppress osteoclast activity when bony alkaline phosphatase is > 2 times the normal level, even without symptoms
claims.quote: In addition, some guidelines (3–5) recommend treatment to: Prevent or slow progression of complications (eg, hearing loss, deformity, osteoarthritis, paraparesis or paraplegia related to vertebral Paget disease, or other neurologic deficits), particularly in a patient for whom surgery is not appropriate Prevent or minimize bleeding if orthopedic surgery is planned at a site with pagetic involvement Suppress excessive osteoclast activity when serum alkaline phosphatase (of bony origin) is > 2 times the normal level, even in the absence of symptoms

claims.text: Medications can slow progression but do not reverse existing deficits (eg, deformity, osteoarthritis, hearing loss, neural impingement)
claims.quote: Although disease progression can be slowed by medications, existing deficits (eg, deformity, osteoarthritis, hearing loss, neural impingement) are not reversed.

claims.text: Ensure adequate intake of calcium and vitamin D; supplements are often needed
claims.quote: Because bone turnover is increased, patients should ensure adequate intake of calcium and vitamin D, and supplements are often needed.
